summary: Tested M2-S03 (validation, built by metadata-builder). Ran both declared checkers verbatim from the build directory exactly as the plan wrote them: check_validation_rules.py at the plan's declared build scope (--manifest-dir artefacts), which printed 'Scanned 1 validation rule(s) across 1 file(s); 0 finding(s) detected.' and exited 0, matching the plan's own fixture description; and check_opportunity_management.py at step scope (--manifest-dir artefacts/M2-S03), which exited 0 with one INFO ('Nothing in this tree is in scope for this checker') because this step's only artefact is a ValidationRule and nothing of the type that checker inspects (stage values, business process, record type definitions, pathAssistants) lives under this step's directory -- recorded honestly as a not-in-scope pass, not as a positive validation of the rule. Also ran the always-on xml parse (2/2 files), the always-on manifest consistency check (ValidationRule named explicitly in package.xml with a file behind it, both directions consistent, no coverage-gap exclusion applies), and check-outputs --hashes (ok, nothing missing/empty/malformed). All four runnable tests passed. The step's two manual acceptance tests were checked against the Given/When/Then shape (both have all three clauses and a directly-inspectable Then) and deferred verbatim to the M2 milestone gate rather than ticked; as a courtesy this run also read the shipped XML against both Then clauses without ticking them, and both hold. results.json written with "passed": true and artefact_hashes from check-outputs --hashes; M2-S03 moved built -> tested via build_plan.py set-status.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran (or was correctly classified as manual), both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly -- the Step 7 HIGH row in agents/step-tester/AGENT.md. No command test was refused, no manifest exclusion had to be applied, and check-outputs reported ok with nothing missing, empty or malformed. The opportunity-management checker's not-in-scope INFO does not itself trigger the MEDIUM row (that row is keyed to a refused command test, a coverage-gap manifest exclusion, or a check-outputs problem, none of which occurred) -- it is reported as a Process Observation instead of a confidence downgrade, per this run's instruction to record it honestly rather than read it as a pass on the rule.

process_observations.observation: check_validation_rules.py exited 0 at the plan's declared build scope and actually resolved every field/permission token the formula names (Discount__c, Approval_Status__c, errorDisplayField, the $Permission token) against M1-S01's fields and M2-S01's custom permission, matching the plan's own fixture description verbatim -- this is a checker that proved something, not merely a green exit.

check_opportunity_management.py's declared test on this step exits 0 with an INFO saying nothing in artefacts/M2-S03/ is in its scope -- the checker was added to this step by amend-step --add-checker on 2026-09-18 to close a §5 coverage warning (the step cites admin/opportunity-management in skills[]), but a validation-rule step has no stage value, business process, record type or pathAssistant for it to inspect. The exit 0 satisfies the declared 'expected: exit 0' and is recorded as a pass, but it validates nothing about this step's actual artefact; a reader of a green test list should not infer the rule's Opportunity-management correctness was checked here.

plan.json's inputs.note for this step states the errorMessage is '129 characters'; the shipped errorMessage (read directly from the deployed XML with ElementTree) is 132 characters. Both are well under the 255-character limit the step's second manual test checks, so the declared expected outcome is unaffected either way, but the discrepancy is in the plan's own prose and worth a human's eye before it is cited as a fact elsewhere.

evidence.detail: errorMessage element, len()==132 vs plan.json steps[M2-S03].inputs.note's '129 characters'
